AN "R. L. CHARLTON" AT NORTHFIELD, 1888 -- AND WHY THE JOIN CANNOT BE MADE
T. J. Shanks, "College Students at Northfield; or, A College of Colleges,
No. 2" (1888). Two Internet Archive scans, both fully downloadable:
collegestudent00shan (Princeton Theological Seminary copy) and
collegestudentsa0000unse. Read 2026-09-07.

=====================================================================
WHAT IS THERE
=====================================================================

Under "CATALOGUE OF DELEGATES. / GENERAL." -- the section for delegates not
attached to a college delegation -- with column headers "Name. / Vocation. /
Address.", the name run reads, in order:

  V. C. Hurt · W. M. Smith · Janzo Kawamoto · F. H. Ibingfield ·
  E. J. Steinity · F. H. Taylor · S. F. Whitehouse · T. H. Taylor ·
  [W.] Moffett · Robert Latt[e] · Stuart L. Roussel · A. Bourquin ·
  W. G. Mills · L. R. Montgomerie · F. H. DuVernet · Cecil C. Owen ·
  Mr. and Mrs. Heard · Alexander Arthur · **R. L. CHARLTON** ·
  Percy E. Judge · R. S. Boss · J. L. Sample · Stuart H. Kyle · ...

and the address run, separately:

  Nanking, China · Florence, Italy · Kobe, Japan · Digby, Eng. · London ·
  " · " · North London, Eng. · New Castle, " · Edinburgh, Scot. ·
  Geneva, Switz. · Lausanne, Switz. · **Kingston, Ont.** · " · " ·
  **Toronto, "** · " · **P. E. I., Canada.** · **Montreal, Que.** · " · " ·
  Dakota Territory. · Bethel, Conn. · London, " · New Haven, Conn. · ...

=====================================================================
WHY THE TWO RUNS CANNOT BE ALIGNED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT
=====================================================================

The scans break the table into three separate column runs, and IN NEITHER DO
THE RUNS HAVE EQUAL LENGTH.

  collegestudent00shan   58 names against about 35 addresses in the same
                         stretch -- roughly twenty-three addresses lost,
                         because the OCR silently drops the repeated ditto
                         marks that stand for "same as above".
  collegestudentsa0000unse  keeps many of the ditto marks as their own lines,
                         which helps, but drops at least one NAME (W. M.
                         Smith, present in the other scan) and garbles several
                         others past recognition.

So counting forward from the top fails, and counting back from the end fails
too, because the discrepancy is distributed through the run rather than at one
end. THIS PROJECT'S OWN RULE FROM THE POSTAL-DIRECTORY WORK APPLIES: the
alignment is checked, not assumed, and here it does not check out. No address
is assigned to Charlton.

=====================================================================
WHAT IS SUGGESTIVE, AND IS NOT EVIDENCE
=====================================================================

A run of CANADIAN addresses -- Kingston, Toronto, Prince Edward Island,
Montreal -- sits a few entries before Charlton's name in both scans. If the
columns ran straight it would put him somewhere just past Montreal.

THEY DO NOT RUN STRAIGHT. Twenty-odd unaligned entries lie in between, and the
addresses immediately after the Canadian run are American (Dakota Territory,
Bethel Conn., New Haven Conn.), so the same loose reasoning would put him in
Connecticut. The suggestion is recorded because it is testable, not because it
is believed.

=====================================================================
WHY ANYONE SHOULD CARE
=====================================================================

Kanawana's R. L. Charlton was a Montreal marine surveyor and "ardent YMCA
worker" of the camp's founding circle, who proposed the name "Kanawana" and
wrote one of the two 1943 manuscript histories of its earliest years. D. L.
Moody's Northfield college conferences were the forge of the student YMCA
movement, and 1888 is SIX YEARS BEFORE the camp. A Montreal YMCA man at
Northfield in 1888 would place the camp's founding circle inside that current
directly rather than by inference.

IT IS ONE PAGE, AND A LEGIBLE IMAGE OF IT SETTLES THIS IN A MINUTE. Both scans
are public; the page is the "GENERAL" table of the Catalogue of Delegates, at
about page 294 of the 1888 edition. What is needed is the page IMAGE, not more
OCR -- the text layer is the thing that has failed here, twice.
